solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Island language for “coffee”

blocks.note: first meaning: the large Indonesian island
second meaning: a slang word used for coffee, chiefly American

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the islanders call coffee in their own tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Language' tempts you towards a tongue spoken on an island (or the programming language); here 'language for' means 'a word for', and the quotation marks show it is the word itself being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indonesian island grew so much coffee that its name became American slang for a cup of the drink.

clue.text: Fairytale beast to outstay welcome?

blocks.note: first meaning: the fire-breathing monster of legend
second meaning, split into two words: to go on tediously for too long

explanation.surface: A fairytale monster that will not leave the party.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as DRAG ON; the question mark admits that a phrasal verb is stretched to mean overstaying.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary winged reptile appears throughout fairy stories, while 'drag on' describes something lasting longer than anyone wants.

clue.text: Hints of its terrible execrations suppressed by parrot considerately

indicators.note: a hint is only a small first trace, so each word contributes just its opening letter
something suppressed is held down inside another, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Polly is the stock name for a pet parrot
the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A parrot is too well-mannered to swear, keeping its terrible curses down to mere hints.
explanation.walkthrough: Polly is the crossword's stock parrot. Execrations are curses, a nice match for a parrot's reputation for picking up bad language.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with good manners and consideration towards others is behaving in a courteous, well-mannered way.

clue.text: Security number: good test for network

blocks.note: a personal identification number guards a bank card
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A note on IT security: choosing a solid number and testing a computer network.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon reads like a list heading but is just punctuation between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ping is a small signal sent to another computer to check whether it is reachable and how quickly it replies.

clue.text: Tedious fight curtailed by fight venue

indicators.note: to curtail is to cut short, originally docking a tail, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: BOX means to fight, then loses its last letter
boxers fight in a ring

explanation.surface: A dull boxing match cut short by the arena itself.
explanation.walkthrough: BOUT is the obvious 'fight', but shortening it leaves BOU; the verb BOX is the one that works. 'By' here just means 'next to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and uninteresting that wearies the listener is described as tiresome or dreary.

clue.text: Go along with disruption of ie, voting

indicators.note: a disruption throws things into disorder, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Going along with a disrupted vote, that is.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray 'ie' looks like the abbreviation for 'that is', but its two letters are simply part of the material to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield or submit to someone's wishes is to comply or accept them rather than resist.

clue.text: Attitude in hotel event shows top style

indicators.note: the word places one thing inside another, so one piece sits within the pair around it

blocks.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
an air is a manner or bearing
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: An attitude on display at a hotel function signals the very best style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like it means 'the best', but it is the top of the head, where hair grows.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairstyle is a way of arranging what grows on your head, the topmost part of the body.

clue.text: Symbolic identifier originally with a pointed shape

indicators.note: what comes originally comes at the start, so only the opening letter counts

blocks.note: the opening letter
cone-shaped, tapering to a point

explanation.surface: A symbol used as an identifier, shaped like a pointed cone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Symbolic identifier' reads as one phrase, like a logo; the definition is the first word alone. 'With a pointed shape' is taken as an adjective, cone-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iconic serves as an emblem or representative image of a wider idea, so it stands for more than itself.

clue.text: Giggling, wriggling gal in hug

indicators.note: wriggling means twisting about, so the letters squirm into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl squirms and giggles while being hugged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal placing one word inside another, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Giggling is a light, silly form of mirth, so it is a kind of chuckling with amusement.

clue.text: Satisfied iodine repelled object

indicators.note: to repel is to drive back, so the letters are sent back the way they came

blocks.note: a demand that is met is satisfied
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A contented chemist watches iodine push something away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satisfied' sounds like a mood, but it is the past tense of a verb, as in requirements met.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single article or thing, one distinct thing among others in a list or collection.

clue.text: Dive exercises to include breathing apparatus?

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: physical education, gym lessons at school
the organ the body breathes with

explanation.surface: Diving training that includes using scuba gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathing apparatus' suggests scuba gear, matching the diving surface; the question mark flags that it is really a body organ.
explanation.definitionFit: To dive is to jump headfirst into water, which is the same as throwing yourself down into it.

clue.text: Fortune to secure a medicine? One’s ineffective

definitions.note: a noun phrase, 'one who is ineffective'

indicators.note: securing something means holding it firmly within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: fortune, good or bad
taken as written
short for medication

explanation.surface: Gambling your fortune on some medicine turns out to be useless.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark splits wordplay from definition; 'One's ineffective' means 'a person who is ineffective'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a weak, helpless person or an official serving out a term after losing power.

clue.text: In preference to grand, a new instrument for the church

blocks.note: OR means 'rather than', as in 'this or that'
G is short for a grand, a thousand
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A church chooses a new instrument rather than a grand piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' plants a grand piano in the reader's mind, which fits the instrument theme, but it gives only one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipe organ is the keyboard instrument traditionally installed to accompany hymns in churches.

clue.text: Old book, mostly outraged, about nothing at all

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
B is the abbreviation for book
LIVID means furious, then loses its last letter
on means concerning, as in a talk on history

explanation.surface: An old book that leaves its reader furious over nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container or reversal signal but is simply ON, meaning 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is the state of utter nothingness or of being completely forgotten, a total void.

clue.text: Canine area of scientific research

blocks.note: first meaning: short for a Labrador retriever dog
second meaning: short for laboratory

explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' reads as an adjective describing the research area, as if studying dogs; it is a noun naming a dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form names both a Labrador retriever, a popular dog breed, and the room where experiments happen.

clue.text: I’m going round part of farmyard in a fog

indicators.note: to go round is to turn about and face the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
the pen where pigs are kept

explanation.surface: Someone wanders round the farmyard, lost in thick fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round' could mean wrapping around the sty, but that gives nonsense; it turns the first piece back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: When the air is full of fog, visibility is poor and the weather is hazy and murky.

clue.text: Dog advert during TV programme

indicators.note: something during an event happens inside it, so one piece falls within the other

blocks.note: a television show
short for advertisement

explanation.surface: A dog food commercial screened in the middle of a TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like the noun for the animal in the advert; it is the verb, to tail someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them persistently, just as a detective tails a suspect closely.

clue.text: Appropriate to invest in trim computer

indicators.note: investing originally meant clothing or wrapping, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: to lop is to cut off or prune
apt means suitable

explanation.surface: It makes sense to buy a slim, lightweight computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' sounds financial, and 'trim' like a slim design; both play other roles. 'Appropriate' is the adjective, not the verb meaning to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal machine small enough to rest on your knees while you use it.

clue.text: Law enforcement staff including one Charlie

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the outer piece takes the others inside it

blocks.note: a staff is a long stick or rod
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is Charlie in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The police force's staff includes an officer called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Law enforcement staff' reads as a single phrase for officers, but 'staff' is the stick. Charlie is also slang for a fool, a distraction here.
explanation.definitionFit: The police are the civil force responsible for upholding the law and keeping public order.

clue.text: I had each brainwave

blocks.note: the contraction I'd, without its apostrophe
EA is the abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having one brilliant inspiration after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I had each brainwave' sounds like a boast; the first two words simply shorten to a contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever thought, so it is a notion or inspiration that pops into the mind.

clue.text: Gallant fellow almost allowed in running race

indicators.note: almost means falling just short, so the final letter is lost
the word places one thing inside another, so one piece sits within the other
running suggests things in motion and out of place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: VALID means permitted or acceptable, then loses its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dashing man is nearly allowed to take part in a running race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running race' looks like one phrase for an athletics event; 'running' is the rearrangement signal for the four letters that wrap the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier was a courtly horseman or gentleman, and the word survives for a chivalrous, dashing man.

clue.text: Cool line in rainwear turning up

indicators.note: the word places one thing inside another, so one piece sits within the other
in a down clue, turning upwards means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a mac (mackintosh) is a British raincoat
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A cool new style of raincoat comes back into fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' suggests fashionable, matching the clothes surface, but here it means composed and unruffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stays cool keeps their composure and remains serene and unflustered under pressure.

clue.text: Issue US magazine promoted

indicators.note: promotion moves things upwards, and in a down clue going up means reading backwards

blocks.note: Time is the American news weekly

explanation.surface: An issue of an American magazine gets advertised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a noun for a magazine edition, fitting the surface, but it is the verb, to give out.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue something is to send it forth or discharge it, as a chimney gives out smoke.

clue.text: Husband boarding small trendy train

indicators.note: to board is to get on or into something, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels
H is the abbreviation for husband
fashionable

explanation.surface: A husband gets on a small, stylish train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like the railway noun, matching 'boarding', but it is the verb meaning to teach.
explanation.definitionFit: To school a person or animal is to teach or drill them in a skill, the same as coaching.

clue.text: Tolkien monster concealed flower

blocks.note: orcs are the brutish creatures in The Lord of the Rings
past tense of hide

explanation.surface: A monster from Middle-earth hides a flower away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concealed' could signal a hidden word, but it simply supplies its synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchid is an exotic bloom with elaborate, often showy petals, prized by gardeners.
